argv:
You generate synthetic meeting transcripts with gold annotations for LiveMinutes, a research dataset modeled on the AMI Meeting Corpus scenario meetings.

In AMI scenario meetings, a team of four plays a design team in a fictional company. The roles are Project Manager (PM), Marketing Expert (ME), User Interface designer (UI) and Industrial Designer (ID). A series has four meetings: (a) kickoff, (b) functional design, (c) conceptual design, (d) detailed design. Later meetings refer back to earlier ones.

Write natural spoken conversation the way AMI transcripts read: short turns, fillers ("um", "uh", "yeah"), backchannels ("mm-hmm", "okay"), interruptions, people building on each other, and some disfluency. Do not write a screenplay. Do not narrate. No stage directions.

Each segment is one dialogue-act-like unit: one speaker, usually one clause or short sentence, sometimes just a backchannel. Give each segment an AMI dialogue-act type from this set:
  bck backchannel, stl stall, fra fragment, inf inform, sug suggest, ass assess,
  el.inf elicit-inform, el.sug elicit-offer-or-suggestion, el.ass elicit-assessment,
  el.und elicit-comment-understanding, off offer, und comment-about-understanding,
  be.pos be-positive, be.neg be-negative, oth other

Absent participants NEVER speak. Speaker labels are ground truth: use only the labels you are given.

The gold annotations must be exactly true of the transcript you write. Refer to segments by their "n" number. Every number you cite must exist.

Output a single JSON object and nothing else: no prose, no markdown fences.

request.user:
Write meeting SY0110c: meeting "c" (conceptual design) of series SY0110.

PROJECT
The team is designing a reusable coffee cup with a deposit system.

PARTICIPANTS (label, role, status for this meeting)
A  Marketing Expert (ME)  Marta  present
B  User Interface designer (UI)  Jonas  present
C  Project Manager (PM)  Priya  present
D  Industrial Designer (ID)  Tom  present

EARLIER MEETINGS IN THIS SERIES
Stay consistent with them. Refer back to them, follow up on their open action items, and keep the same product and team.

[SY0110a, kickoff]
  abstract: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting, introduced herself, and the industrial designer and user interface designer introduced themselves. The marketing expert was absent because she was attending a hospitality trade fair in Cologne, and the team saw this as a chance to gather input from cafe owners there. The project manager presented the project: a reusable coffee cup with a deposit system, sold to cafes, where end users pay a deposit and return the cup to any partner cafe to get it back. Management's constraints are a deposit of one euro per cup, a production cost under three euros per cup, and a target of fifty partner cafes in the first year. The industrial designer raised durability in hot industrial dishwashers and suggested a collapsible silicone cup, while the user interface designer raised the question of how cups are returned and suggested a tracking app with a QR code; neither idea was adopted. The team agreed that the cup must be dishwasher-safe and fit standard takeaway lid sizes, and distributed research tasks ahead of the functional design meeting.
  decisions: The cup must be dishwasher-safe. The cup must fit the standard takeaway lid sizes cafes already use. The tracking app idea is on hold until the marketing expert's findings are available.
  actions: The industrial designer will research durable, dishwasher-safe materials within the three-euro production cost and bring options to the next meeting. The user interface designer will investigate the return process and how existing deposit systems handle it. The marketing expert (absent) is to talk to cafe owners at the trade fair about whether they would join a deposit system and what they would want from it. The project manager will write up the minutes and send them to the marketing expert together with her task.
  problems: With a one-euro deposit and a production cost of up to three euros, lost cups could be costly for cafes; the team left open how to address this. Whether a collapsible silicone design is viable remains open, given cleaning concerns. The return mechanism (counter, machine or app) has not been decided.
  action item SY0110a.ai1: Research durable, dishwasher-safe materials that keep production cost under three euros per cup and bring options to the next meeting. (owner D, active)
  action item SY0110a.ai2: Investigate the cup return process and how existing deposit systems let customers get their deposit back. (owner B, active)
  action item SY0110a.ai3: Talk to cafe owners at the trade fair about whether they would join a deposit system and what they would want from it. (owner A, active)
  action item SY0110a.ai4: Send the meeting minutes and her task to the absent marketing expert. (owner C, reassigned)
  fact (absence): The marketing expert (Marta) was absent because she was attending a hospitality trade fair in Cologne, booked before the project started.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The industrial designer proposed a collapsible silicone cup; the user interface designer raised cleaning concerns and it was kept only as an idea.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer proposed an app that tracks cups via a QR code on the bottom; it was not adopted.

[SY0110b, functional design]
  abstract: The project manager opened the functional design meeting, welcomed back the marketing expert, who had been at the Cologne trade fair during the kickoff, and recapped the requirements from the kickoff: the cup must be dishwasher-safe and fit standard takeaway lids, with a one-euro deposit, a production cost under three euros and fifty partner cafes in the first year. On the cup itself, the industrial designer compared stainless steel (about 3.80 euros, over budget), bamboo fibre (melamine-bound and unsuitable for hot dishwashers), collapsible silicone (about 2.60 euros, but hard to clean and the flexing rim does not hold a lid) and polypropylene (about 1.20 euros and dishwasher-proof). The team chose polypropylene and dropped the silicone idea. Based on the cafe owners' feedback reported by the marketing expert, the cup will be stackable with a tapered shape, have a 90 mm rim to fit the common lid size, and have space for a cafe logo. On returns, the user interface designer compared supermarket bottle machines with existing cup schemes and recommended a counter return at any partner cafe, where staff refund the euro. The tracking app stays shelved, which matches the cafe owners' wish for no extra steps at the counter. Return machines and a two-euro deposit were both suggested and rejected. To show customers where they can return cups, the team liked the idea of a partner badge in cafe windows that matches the logo on the cup. The team discussed lost cups again: with polypropylene, a cafe loses only about twenty cents per unreturned cup. For the dishwasher durability test, the team first agreed on the office dishwasher but then revised the plan. The final plan is to run the samples for a week in the commercial dishwasher of Café Lindner, a cafe owner the marketing expert met at the fair.
  decisions: The cup will be made of polypropylene; the collapsible silicone idea is dropped. The cup will have a 90 mm rim to fit standard lids, will be stackable, and will have space for a cafe logo. Cups will be returned at the counter of any partner cafe, where staff refund the deposit; there will be no app and no return machines. The deposit stays at one euro. Partner cafes will be marked with a window badge that matches the logo on the cup. The dishwasher test will run for a week at Café Lindner (revised from the original plan to test in the office dishwasher on Thursday).
  actions: The industrial designer will prepare polypropylene samples by Monday and run the dishwasher durability test at Café Lindner for a week. The marketing expert will email the owner of Café Lindner this week to arrange the test. The marketing expert will write up her notes from the trade fair and send them round. The user interface designer will sketch the counter return flow and the partner badge for the next meeting. The project manager will write the minutes.
  problems: Cafes still lose about twenty cents for every cup that is not returned; who absorbs this has not been settled. Polypropylene must still prove its durability in the commercial dishwasher test. The test depends on the owner of Café Lindner confirming the arrangement.
  action item SY0110b.ai1: Prepare polypropylene cup samples and run a week-long dishwasher durability test at Café Lindner (originally planned for the office dishwasher on Thursday). (owner D, active)
  action item SY0110b.ai2: Contact the owner of Café Lindner to arrange the dishwasher test. (owner A, active)
  action item SY0110b.ai3: Sketch the counter return flow and the partner badge for the next meeting. (owner B, active)
  action item SY0110b.ai4: Write up the notes from the trade fair and send them round to the team. (owner A, active)
  action item SY0110b.ai5: Write the meeting minutes. (owner C, active)
  fact (plan_change): The team first agreed that the industrial designer would test samples in the office dishwasher on Thursday, then changed the plan to a week-long test in Café Lindner's commercial dishwasher.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The industrial designer proposed raising the deposit to two euros; this was rejected because management fixed it at one euro and cafe owners found two euros too high.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested return machines in busier cafes; this was rejected because of cost and counter space.

EDGE CASES THIS MEETING MUST CONTAIN
Weave each one naturally into the project discussion. Each must be clearly present, and each must be tagged with the segments where it happens.
- F1_SARCASM_AS_FACT [F1]: Someone makes a joke or sarcastic remark phrased as a statement of fact (e.g. "great, so we'll just make it out of solid gold"), and the team does not adopt it. The gold summary must NOT report the joke as a decision or fact.
  Required gold labels: summary, edge_cases.
- F1_OFF_TOPIC_TANGENT [F1]: A long off-topic tangent (at least 8 consecutive segments, e.g. weekend plans, a film, the coffee machine) unrelated to the project. The gold summary must NOT include the tangent's content.
  Required gold labels: summary, edge_cases.

LENGTH
Between 90 and 140 segments.

GOLD LABELS
- summary: AMI-style abstractive summary in third person, using role names ("The project manager ..."). Sections: abstract (3-6 sentences), actions, decisions, problems (open issues). It reflects the meeting's FINAL state: corrected values, final plans, and no jokes or tangents reported as content.
- action_items: every task arising in the meeting. owner is the speaker label of the FINAL owner, and may be an absent participant. owner is null ONLY for a task nobody takes, with owner_unclear true. status is the final status: active, reassigned (owner changed; previous_owners lists earlier owners) or dropped. history lists the events in order. evidence_segments lists the supporting segments.
- qa_facts: atomic facts someone could later ask about ("Who was asked to ...?", "Did the team agree on ...?"). Include every decision (agreed true), every proposal nobody agreed to (type unagreed_proposal, agreed false), action items, removed action items, absences, and plan changes. Because this meeting follows earlier ones, include at least one fact of type reference_to_prior_meeting, with refers_to_meeting set, at a point where someone refers back to an earlier meeting. Do NOT write questions.
- edge_cases: one entry per edge case above, with its scenario_id and the segment numbers that contain it.

OUTPUT JSON SHAPE
{
  "segments": [{"n": 1, "speaker": "A", "da_type": "inf", "text": "..."}],
  "summary": {"abstract": ["..."], "actions": ["..."], "decisions": ["..."], "problems": ["..."]},
  "action_items": [{"n": 1, "description": "...", "owner": "C", "owner_unclear": false, "status": "active", "previous_owners": [], "history": [{"segment": 12, "event": "assigned", "by": "A", "owner": "C"}], "evidence_segments": [12, 13]}],
  "qa_facts": [{"type": "decision", "fact": "...", "agreed": true, "related_action_item": null, "refers_to_meeting": null, "evidence_segments": [40]}],
  "edge_cases": [{"scenario_id": "...", "segments": [20, 21, 22], "note": "one line on how it appears"}]
}
history events: proposed, offered, assigned, accepted, reassigned, dropped, restated. qa_facts types: decision, unagreed_proposal, action_item, action_item_removed, absence, plan_change, reference_to_prior_meeting, other. related_action_item is an action item's "n" or null. refers_to_meeting is an earlier meeting ID of this series or null.
